title: Thou, Lord, Who Rear'st the Mountain's Height
description: Thou, Lord, Who Rear'st the Mountain's Height in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Sterling wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 303, “Divine Meaning in Humble Things”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou, Lord, who rear'st the moun-tain's height, And mak'st the cliffs with sun-shine bright; O, grant that we may own Thy hand No less in ev-ery grain of sand!

lines: Thou, Lord, who rear'st the mountain's height,
And mak'st the cliffs with sunshine bright;
O, grant that we may own Thy hand
No less in every grain of sand!
With forests huge, of dateless time,
Thy will has hung each peak sublime;
But withered leaves beneath the tree
Have tongues that tell as loud of Thee.
Teach us that not a leaf can grow,
Till life from Thee within it flow;
That not a grain of dust can be,
O Fount of being! save by Thee;
That every human word and deed,
Each flash of feeling, will, or creed,
Begun and ended all in love.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Sterling died in 1844.
credits: Words by John Sterling (1806–1844), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
